new_statements.quote: Unsur suprasegmental bahasa Ranau seperti nada, tekanan, tempo tidak bersifat fonemik pada tataran kata. Mungkin aspek suprasegmental terdapat pada tataran kalimat, tetapi aspek kalimat pada kesempatan ini tidak menjadi objek penelitian. Oleh karena itu, kalaupun terdapat fonem suprasegmental pada tataran kalimat, tidak dapat terdeteksi melalui penelitian ini karena penelitian ini hanya terbatas pada aspek fonologi dan morfologi.
new_statements.translation: Suprasegmental elements of the Ranau language such as pitch, stress and tempo are not phonemic at the word level. Suprasegmental aspects may exist at the sentence level, but the sentence level is not an object of the present study. Therefore, even if suprasegmental phonemes exist at the sentence level, they cannot be detected by this study, because it is limited to phonology and morphology.
new_statements.citation: Arifin, Siti Salamah; Tarmizi Abubakar; Ernalida; Ansori Z.A; Marzuan. 1998. Fonologi dan Morfologi Bahasa Ranau. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. ISBN 979-459-822-4.
new_statements.locator: Bab III Fonologi, sec. 3.6 'Aspek Suprasegmental', p. 42 (PDF page 54 of the repository scan)
new_statements.reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (216 pp., Acrobat Paper Capture text layer). Rendered PDF page 54 at 100 dpi and read it: the page is numbered 42 at the top and carries 3.5 Gugus Konsonan, 3.6 Aspek Suprasegmental and the start of 3.7 Struktur Suku Kata. The quoted paragraph is there verbatim: 'Unsur suprasegmental bahasa Ranau seperti nada, tekanan, tempo tidak bersifat fonemik pada tataran kata. Mungkin aspek suprasegmental terdapat pada tataran kalimat, tetapi aspek kalimat pada kesempatan ini tidak menjadi objek penelitian. Oleh karena itu, kalaupun terdapat fonem suprasegmental pada tataran kalimat, tidak dapat terdeteksi melalui penelitian ini karena penelitian ini hanya terbatas pada aspek fonologi dan morfo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only Ranau-specific description says stress (with pitch and tempo) is not phonemic/contrastive at the word level and gives no position for it; it neither asserts nor denies a phonetic word stress. The nearest positional statement for the same language (Lampung Api) is Walker 1976 for the Way Lima Pesisir dialect: slight, non-contrastive stress on the final syllable of every word, derived or not, clitics unstressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in Arifin et al. 1998; not mentioned by Walker 1976 either.
new_statements.exceptions: None in Arifin et al. 1998. Walker 1976 fn. 13 (Way Lima, not Ranau): a few non-Lampung place names (Palembang, Jakarta, Indonesia) have penultimate stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('pada tataran kata'); sentence-level prosody explicitly excluded from the study. Data are elicited citation forms from adult native speakers of one 'original' geographic variety in Kecamatan Banding Agung (sec. 1.5, 2.1).
new_statements.identity_note: rana1249 is a Glottolog Bookkeeping code for retired ISO 639-3 [rae] Ranau, merged into Lampung Api [ljp] (lamp1243) by CR 2007-142 (adopted 2008-01-14); Glottolog now lists Ranau as dialect rana1248 of Lampung Api. The quoted source (Arifin et al. 1998) describes exactly this variety: 'bahasa Ranau' of Kecamatan Banding Agung, Kabupaten Ogan Komering Ulu (now OKU Selatan), South Sumatra, from dusun Sukanegeri (Mekakau, Muara Dua) to Kota Batu (Lampung Barat); the authors treat it as distinct from Komering on speaker self-identification and say it has no internal dialects (sec. 2.2). The final-stress statement in Walker 1976 belongs to a different Lampung Api dialect (Way Lima, southern Pesisir) and should not be attributed to Ranau. Check whether lamp1243 already carries a catalog entry before adding a separate Ranau line.

sources.note: Sec. 3.6 'Aspek Suprasegmental' (printed p. 42, PDF page 54, verified on the rendered page image): pitch, stress and tempo are not phonemic at the word level; sentence-level suprasegmentals were outside the study. No statement of where stress falls; no other mention of tekanan/aksen in the 216 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent the scanned layer).

sources.note: Contains Ranau (Pilla) wordlist reflexes throughout, but states in sec. 6.3 that 'Accent and word-stress has not been treated at all or factored into reconstructions.'

sources.citation: Walker, Dale F. 1976. A Grammar of the Lampung Language: the Pesisir Dialect of Way Lima. NUSA 2. Jakarta: Badan Penyelenggara Seri NUSA. 59 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 5 sec. 2.41: 'Words, both derived and non-derived, are stressed on the final syllable. This word stress, however, is very slight, and it is often skewed by the position of the word in the intonation contour. The word stress is not contrastive.' Fn. 13 p. 48: a few non-Lampung place names have penultimate stress. Clitics unstressed (2.42). Describes the Way Lima 'southern Pesisir' dialect, not Ranau (Walker's own dialect diagram p. 1 places Ranau nowhere; CR 2007-142 says Walker 1975 subsumed Ranau under Krui).
